Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the demo last week — team is excited to move forward. Procurement has started the vendor enrollment in Ariba and I received an automated invite (attached). Before I accept, a couple of quick questions so we don’t get stuck later:

- What exact PO fields do you require coming from Ariba (PO number, ship-to, bill-to, GL code, project code)? Any required field names that we must map to your order form?
- Do you need a specific AP email or invoice routing instructions?
- Our legal asked if Redwood can accept our standard PO terms (we typically push a few warranty/indemnity items into the PO). We also saw an Order Form draft in the portal — would you prefer we redline the order form or sign your standard?

I’ve attached the Ariba invite export and a sample PO from our finance team. Can your team share a short checklist so our onboarding team can finish registration cleanly?

Thanks,

Subject: Re: NewLeaf procurement: Ariba invite and Order Form questions

Rajiv — great to hear and thanks for sending the invite. Short answers up front, then next steps below.

PO fields we require (minimum): PO Number, PO Line Item qty, Unit Price, Currency, Bill-to (name + address), Ship-to/Service Location, Invoice Email, and a reference to our Redwood Sales Order number. Optional but helpful: Cost Center / Project Code. I’ve attached an .xlsx that maps our Order Form fields to common Ariba field names.

AP / invoice routing: please have invoices sent to invoices@redwood.com and include the PO number on the first page header. If NewLeaf needs invoices routed to a specific regional AP email, include a cc when you submit so we can confirm auto-routing.

Order Form / redlines: please redline the Order Form in the portal or attach a redline PDF — either works. We prefer to keep the MSA as-is for now and negotiate limited Order Form edits for billing/term nuances. That said, we’ll loop Legal on any substantive liability or data clauses. I’ve attached our working redline (OrderForm_v2_redline.pdf) with a few notes in the billing section — mostly field-level clarifications for Ariba.

Next steps I can own:
- Laura (cc) will validate PO field mapping against your Ariba schema and share a short checklist to finish enrollment.
- Dev will review any redlines from a legal standpoint and call out must-haves vs negotiables.
- If helpful, we can run a 30-minute alignment call with procurement + IT to confirm the vendor setup and invoice flow so Ariba sends us valid POs.

Proposed times: Fri 4/30 10:00–10:30 or Mon 5/3 09:00–09:30 PT — what works for you?

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

On Wed, Apr 28, 2026 at 11:03 AM Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com> wrote:
> Rajiv — great to hear and thanks for sending the invite....

Rajiv / team — quick legal notes after a skim of the OrderForm_v2_redline.pdf and the sample PO you attached:

1) Liability/cap: Redwood cannot accept an unlimited liability clause on an Order Form. Propose a mutual cap tied to fees paid in the prior 12 months (or a fixed $1M cap for year-one pilots).
2) Data residency & retention: we agree to the data handling terms listed in our MSA; for any specific retention longer than 90 days, we’ll need a JIRA to track a compliance exception.
3) PO-only terms: we can accept payment-term language in a PO (net 45/60) but any change to intellectual property, indemnity, or warranties must be addressed in the MSA — please do not embed contradictory clauses in a PO.
4) SOC2 / audits: NewLeaf asked for SOC2. We will provide our SOC2 Type II summary and can schedule an evidence call; Laura, please attach the SOC2 redacted report or link.

I’ve summarized the non-negotiable items and proposed language in Legal_redline_summary.docx (attached). If NewLeaf wants a redline back to your PO template, we can prepare one but would prefer changes be consolidated into a single Order Form redline to avoid mismatched PO clauses.

Evelyn — if the customer wants to proceed quickly, propose we run the Ariba mapping, accept the vendor invite, and sign the Order Form with the agreed liability cap. Legal can then iterate on any remaining language in parallel.

- Dev
Dev Patel
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
attachments: Legal_redline_summary.docx
